name: Ramipril
summary: A long-acting ACE inhibitor prodrug whose HOPE trial showed cardiovascular-event reduction in high-risk patients without left ventricular dysfunction — the prototype 'vascular protection' ACE inhibitor.
mechanism: Prodrug hydrolyzed to ramiprilat, which inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, lowering angiotensin II and increasing bradykinin.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic ester hydrolysis to active ramiprilat

dosing.adult: 2.5 mg once daily initially, titrated to 5–10 mg once daily (HOPE regimen 10 mg/day)

safety.pregnancy: Contraindicated in second and third trimesters (fetotoxic)
warnings: Angioedema — potentially life-threatening, highest in Black patients
Rise in creatinine in renal-artery stenosis

indications: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
Cardiovascular risk reduction in high-risk patients (HOPE)
clinicalPearls: HOPE: ramipril 10 mg daily cut cardiovascular death, MI, and stroke in patients at high risk with preserved LV function — the basis of its 'vascular protection' reputation.
Cough is bradykinin-mediated; switching to an ARB is the standard move when it appears.
good: High-CV-risk patients, post-MI, HFrEF, and diabetic nephropathy.
bad: Angioedema history, pregnancy, or bilateral renal artery stenosis.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard pharmacology references (Goodman & Gilman, Katzung, Lexicomp-level standard facts). Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
